question.problem: If ${log}_{125}⁡x=\frac{{log}_{5}⁡x}{k},$ where $k$ is an integer, then $k=${{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
We use the change of base formula:

$$
{log}_{a}⁡X=\frac{{log}_{b}⁡X}{{log}_{b}⁡a}
$$

We want to change from base $a=125$ to base $b=5.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{125}⁡x & =\frac{{log}_{5}⁡x}{{log}_{5}⁡125}.\end{aligned}
$$

Rewriting the expression in the denominator using exponents, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{log}_{5}⁡x}{{log}_{5}⁡125} & =\frac{{log}_{5}⁡x}{{log}_{5}⁡({5}^{3})} \\  & =\frac{{log}_{5}⁡x}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
{log}_{125}⁡x=\frac{{log}_{5}⁡x}{3}.
$$

Hence, $k=3.$
